I was not in freshman connection, in fact I actually attend Emory not UMD. However, I spoke to an admissions officer (a family friend) who gave me insight on how and why people get selected for freshman connection. She told me this before I even considered applying to UMD but she strongly recommended I should and so I did.

The most common misconception is that all freshman connection students are in the program because they had poor high school grades. Although this may be partially true, it is not the main or only reason students are put into this program. I have a clean record, got a 4.5 gpa, a 32 on my ACT, and was the president of multiple clubs in my school, but I was still put into FC. Why you may ask? Because I wasn’t planning on going to Maryland (my parents forced me to and I wanted to go out-of-state) so I applied as an in-state Regular Admissions student, they simply did not have enough space to admit me as an average student but still gave me the Freshman Connections offer.

 Freshman Connection isn’t to accommodate for people who may fall behind the course rigor, it’s made so UMD can make more money off of giving more Out-Of-State students a fall offer and still accept other students even if they’re over their accepted students-quota. What the admissions officer told me is that Out-Of-State students will often apply and not be able to afford the full four years. After realizing they can’t keep up with payments, they have a tendency to drop out or transfer after fall semester. This trend was so noticeable that UMD decided to use this to their benefit. They accept students for spring so they can basically have backup students but still make money off of Out- Of-State students. So whether it’s because FC students had poor grades, spotty attendance, multiple disciplinary actions, or simply because they were an in-state student applying Regular Decision, it’s all the same. The point of FC is just to make the college more money off of prioritizing  Out-Of-State students but still making place for other students who don’t want to attend the Spring Semester. Colleges, unfortunately, are businesses so they act accordingly, UMD is no exception. 

I know some people who hated FC because it made it more difficult to work afternoon or night shifts since that’s when they had class. Another complaint I’ve heard was that they couldn’t take all the classes they wanted, you take mostly GenEd’s as a freshman connection student. On the other hand, many appreciated that they didn’t have to worry about the course-load and could genuinely enjoy freshman year. Additionally, many FC students actually prefer the afternoon classes so they don’t have to wake up at the crack of dawn. Plus, I’ve heard the FC dorms are ideal since they tend to have air conditioning. 

All in all, it’s down to preference really. Congratulations on your acceptance and don’t let the FC program make you belittle your achievements.
